items.grounds: Re-derived from bytes, both ways. MT 56:4 opens כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.56.4, byte tier): the conjunction is token 1 and the formula tokens 2-4, so the row's statement that the 56:4 formula is not verse-initial and stands after a subordinating conjunction is byte-true. MT 52:3 opens כִּֽי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.52.3, byte tier) and MT 52:4 opens כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Isa.52.4, byte tier), the same construction at skeleton tier. Sweep of the skeleton כי כה אמר (skeleton tier): 14 verses, 14 tokens, word-bound and substring counts agreeing, so the finding's digit re-derives; but its 'one object book-wide' framing blends the role split the hazard catalog forbids blending: MT 36:16 is one of the 14 and is a royal-messenger site per the koh-amar census (royal sites exactly 36:4, 36:14, 36:16, 37:3), standing mid-verse, while the divine-frame verse-initial object stands in 13 verses (8:11, 18:4, 21:6, 21:16, 30:15, 31:4, 45:18, 49:25, 52:3, 52:4, 56:4, 57:15, 66:12), the three named among them. What is verifiable against the shipped row: no field names a principle that lets a conjunction-prefixed formula reinforce an open frame here while opening one elsewhere, although a byte-visible discriminator sits in the row's own span and goes unstated: the formula's addressee לַסָּֽרִיסִים֙ (oshb:Isa.56.4, byte tier) resumes the party the preceding verse quotes, וְאַל יֹאמַר֙ הַסָּרִ֔יס (oshb:Isa.56.3, byte tier), a lexical tie on the skeleton סריס (oshb:Isa.56.3 and oshb:Isa.56.4, skeleton tier; sweep: 3 verses book-wide, 39:7, 56:3, 56:4), and the frame-owner is the same tetragrammaton form at כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.56.1, byte tier) and 56:4, whereas 52:4 shifts to the adonai-YHWH form. Tested against the neighbor evidence readable here, the row's treatment is coherent rather than incoherent: the row shipping MT 57:14-57:21 in this slice's context likewise declines to open at the conjunction-prefixed frame כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר רָ֣ם וְנִשָּׂ֗א (oshb:Isa.57.15, byte tier). The cross-row half of the claim, that the rows shipping MT 52:3-52:4 treat this construction as a fresh onset at 52:3|52:4, cannot be re-derived here: those rows lie outside this slice's context and no exact path to them was supplied, so that assertion stands on the auditor's report alone; the mark inventory keys only a SAMEKH at MT 52:2 (single-witness, tier-3) near that seam and no seg at 52:3 or 52:4. On the evidence in hand the surviving defect is an unstated discriminating principle inside a warrant that is byte-true and not load-bearing, since the hold across 56:3 and 56:4 also rests on the byte-identical refrain pairs the row discloses, שֹׁמֵ֤ר שַׁבָּת֙ מֵֽחַלְּל֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.56.2 and oshb:Isa.56.6, byte tier; 2 verses book-wide) and וּמַחֲזִיקִ֖ים בִּבְרִיתִֽי (oshb:Isa.56.4 and oshb:Isa.56.6, byte tier; 2 verses book-wide). That is a disclosure shortfall: low, not medium. The proposed field repair (state the principle, or route the pair for one ruling) stands as a disclosure repair.

Re-derived against the mark inventory at MT keys (its face declares the single witness WLC and MT numbering): SAMEKH keyed at Isa.55.13, Isa.56.2, Isa.56.3 and Isa.56.5 with no PE among them, exactly one paseq seg keyed at Isa.56.4, and a ketiv/qere note at Isa.55.13 that the row also discloses; every mark claim in the row is content-true and type-true, and the paseq is cited count-only as the inventory requires. The defect is real and exactly as described: boundary_evidence_refs carries all five mark entries under the web: prefix while device_notes cites the same paseq as oshb:Isa.56.4, so the witness and numbering-space attribution is internally inconsistent. It is mechanical here. Chapters 55-56 are identity chapters, so each web: coordinate crosswalks to the same MT key and the claims validate at MT keys after that mapping; marks are tier-3 corroboration that never drive a seam, the row says so in its own words, and no digit, type or position is wrong. The habit is part-wide rather than this row's own: the same web:-prefixed mark form recurs in the book-order neighbor rows readable in this slice's context ('web:Isa.56.9 (setumah, single-witness)' in the 56:9 row, 'web:Isa.57.14 (setumah, single-witness)' and 'web:Isa.57.21 (setumah, single-witness)' in the 57:14 row, 'web:Isa.58.14 (setumah, single-witness)' in the 59:1 row), so the finding's supporting statement that every other row cites marks under oshb: is not borne out by the rows readable here, and the convention evidently passed the Tier-0 mark validators. The offset-zone hazard the finding invokes is counterfactual for these coordinates. Under the severity law a prefix mis-attribution on non-driving corroboration objects whose content re-derives is a mechanical disclosure shortfall: low, not a defective mark claim. The proposed re-prefixing of the five refs entries and the four bare device_notes refs to oshb: stands.

MT 57:14 opens verse-initially on וְאָמַ֥ר (oshb:Isa.57.14, byte tier), the waw-plus-perfect third-person-singular speech-introduction verb that both witnesses carry as 'He will say' (web:Isa.57.14); the verse continues סֹֽלּוּ סֹ֖לּוּ פַּנּוּ דָ֑רֶךְ (oshb:Isa.57.14, byte tier), so the row's rear-seam claim is byte-true. The shipped row's boundary_evidence_refs carries web:Isa.57.14 but no oshb:Isa.57.14 while pairing oshb refs for 57:3, 57:4, 57:6, 57:7, 57:13 and 57:15, and boundary_rationale quotes no Hebrew for the seam driver; the book-order neighbor row opening at 57:14 splices the same form at byte tier. The mark inventory keys no seg at MT 57:13 (the next keyed seg is the SAMEKH at 57:14), so the seam has no tier-3 corroboration and rests on this verb-form onset alone. The engagement-class law makes a pointed splice plus tier label mandatory for every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim; a load-bearing seam driver carried on the English witness alone is a defective warrant, not a mechanical shortfall, and the byte-truth of the claim keeps the boundary itself sound, so nothing rises to high. Medium as filed. The proposed field repair (splice the form beside the WEB citation and add oshb:Isa.57.14) stands, with no seam movement.

Re-derived token by token at byte tier, with no morphology layer staged, so form classes are read from the pointed bytes and both witnesses' renderings as the campaign requires. First-person-plural finite verbs stand at נְקַוֶּ֤ה and נְהַלֵּֽךְ (oshb:Isa.59.9), נְגַֽשְׁשָׁ֤ה, נְגַשֵּׁ֑שָׁה, כָּשַׁ֤לְנוּ (oshb:Isa.59.10), נֶהֱמֶ֤ה, נֶהְגֶּ֑ה, נְקַוֶּ֤ה (oshb:Isa.59.11), and last at יְדַֽעֲנֽוּם (oshb:Isa.59.12), 'we know them' (web:Isa.59.12). MT 59:13 carries no finite first-person form: פָּשֹׁ֤עַ וְכַחֵשׁ֙, וְנָס֖וֹג, דַּבֶּר and הֹר֧וֹ וְהֹג֛וֹ (oshb:Isa.59.13, byte tier) are infinitive-absolute forms, rendered participially as 'transgressing and denying Yahweh, and turning away ... speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving and uttering' (web:Isa.59.13), and the verse's only first-person element is the plural suffix on אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ (oshb:Isa.59.13, byte tier). MT 59:14, וְהֻסַּ֤ג אָחוֹר֙ מִשְׁפָּ֔ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה מֵרָח֣וֹק תַּעֲמֹ֑ד כִּֽי כָשְׁלָ֤ה בָֽרְחוֹב֙ אֱמֶ֔ת וּנְכֹחָ֖ה לֹא תוּכַ֥ל לָבֽוֹא (oshb:Isa.59.14, byte tier), carries no first-person form of any kind: וְהֻסַּ֤ג (oshb:Isa.59.14, byte tier) is a passive third-person waw-perfect and תַּעֲמֹ֑ד, כָשְׁלָ֤ה and תוּכַ֥ל (oshb:Isa.59.14, byte tier) are third-person feminine forms, matching 'Justice is turned away backward ... uprightness can't enter.' (web:Isa.59.14). The row's sentence that the confession 'continues in first-person-plural verb forms through web:Isa.59.9-Isa.59.14' is therefore byte-false for its last two verses, exactly as filed, while the row's own splices stop at 59:12. The defect is not load-bearing: the front seam rests on the person shift at עַל כֵּ֗ן רָחַ֤ק מִשְׁפָּט֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ (oshb:Isa.59.9, byte tier) and the rear seam on the wayyiqtol onset וַתְּהִ֤י הָֽאֱמֶת֙ נֶעְדֶּ֔רֶת (oshb:Isa.59.15, byte tier), both of which re-derive. MT 59:13 continues the confession as the object catalogue of 59:12's 'we know them', which is the ground the repair should state for it. Medium as filed; the proposed restriction of the form claim to 59:9-59:12 with separate grounds for 59:13-59:14 stands.

MT 59:8 is sixteen tokens: דֶּ֤רֶךְ שָׁלוֹם֙ לֹ֣א יָדָ֔עוּ וְאֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּ֖ט בְּמַעְגְּלוֹתָ֑ם נְתִיבֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ עִקְּשׁ֣וּ לָהֶ֔ם כֹּ֚ל דֹּרֵ֣ךְ בָּ֔הּ לֹ֥א יָדַ֖ע שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Isa.59.8, byte tier). The phrase וְאֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּ֖ט stands as tokens five and six, immediately before the athnach-bearing בְּמַעְגְּלוֹתָ֑ם (oshb:Isa.59.8, byte tier), and the verse closes on לֹ֥א יָדַ֖ע שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Isa.59.8, byte tier); the finding's own position digit is off by one (it says fourth and fifth), but its claim is byte-true: the phrase is mid-verse before the caesura, not verse-closing. The device_notes sentence applies 'closing the verse' to both members of its bracket, and that is true only of the partner: אֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּֽט (oshb:Isa.59.15, byte tier) is tokens twelve and thirteen of thirteen, verse-final. The digits re-derive at skeleton tier: אין משפט (skeleton tier) in 2 verses book-wide, 59:8 and 59:15, 2 tokens; the justice noun משפט (skeleton tier, substring sweep) in 40 verses book-wide, 42 tokens, 5 verses in this chapter (59:8, 59:9, 59:11, 59:14, 59:15). The mis-stated position is a byte-false claim inside a texture disclosure that the row itself says moves neither seam, so it is not load-bearing. Medium as filed; the proposed correction to mid-verse before that verse's own caesura, digits kept as swept, stands.

MT 61:4 reads וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם שֹׁמְמ֥וֹת רִֽאשֹׁנִ֖ים יְקוֹמֵ֑מוּ וְחִדְּשׁוּ֙ עָ֣רֵי חֹ֔רֶב שֹׁמְמ֖וֹת דּ֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier): three third-person-plural verbs, וּבָנוּ֙, יְקוֹמֵ֑מוּ and וְחִדְּשׁוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier), with no nominal subject anywhere in the verse, and the nearest plural antecedent is the dative party of וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ אֵילֵ֣י הַצֶּ֔דֶק (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier), the mourners renamed 'trees of righteousness' (web:Isa.61.3); 'They will rebuild the old ruins.' (web:Isa.61.4) names no other referent in either witness. So the row's 'changed subject ... distinct from the mourners just named' is not stated by the bytes and runs against the nearest antecedent chain, as filed. The row's construction-class warrant is non-discriminating by its own wording: וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier) is a waw-plus-perfect finite clause and וּבָנוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier) another, which the row itself calls 'a further waw-plus-perfect clause'; the row also labels the mourners that clause's subject when the bytes make them its dative. The seam is not thereby shown wrong: the purpose-infinitive chain governed by שְׁלָחַ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Isa.61.1, byte tier) does end at 61:3, since 61:4 opens on a finite form and not an infinitive, and the commissioned speaker's first-person forms עָלָ֑י, אֹתִ֜י and שְׁלָחַ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Isa.61.1, byte tier) have no counterpart in 61:4-61:9, where the only first-person elements are the plural suffix on אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ (oshb:Isa.61.6, byte tier) and the divine self-declaration אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.61.8, byte tier), objects the replacement warrant must name as distinct from the speaker's voice. The mark inventory keys no seg at MT 61:4; the paseq at 61:3 is count-only. A defective warrant beside a surviving byte-true ground, not alone load-bearing: medium as filed. The proposed re-argument from the first-person commission frame, with observed_substrate_signals, unit_type, rejected_alternative and confidence treated as dependent fields, stands as a field repair with no seam movement.

The shipped row's front-seam sentence asserts that וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier) 'opens a report' and gives no reason it opens a unit; boundary_evidence_refs carries neither oshb:Isa.61.3 nor web:Isa.61.3, and MT 61:3 is never quoted or named. Re-derived: MT 61:3 closes on the finite waw-plus-perfect clause וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ אֵילֵ֣י הַצֶּ֔דֶק מַטַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier), so 'a finite third-person-plural clause' does not by itself discriminate 61:4 from the verse before it; MT 61:4, וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם שֹׁמְמ֥וֹת רִֽאשֹׁנִ֖ים יְקוֹמֵ֑מוּ וְחִדְּשׁוּ֙ עָ֣רֵי חֹ֔רֶב שֹׁמְמ֖וֹת דּ֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier), carries no vocative, imperative, messenger formula, wayyiqtol or explicit addressee change; and the mark inventory keys no seg at 61:4 and only a count-only paseq at 61:3, the nearest SAMEKH segs being keyed at 60:22 and 61:9. The seam itself survives on a ground this row never states: the commissioned speaker's first-person forms עָלָ֑י, אֹתִ֜י and שְׁלָחַ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Isa.61.1, byte tier) and the purpose infinitives they govern end at 61:3, and nothing in 61:4-61:9 resumes that voice (the plural suffix on אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ (oshb:Isa.61.6, byte tier) and the divine first person אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.61.8, byte tier) are distinct objects). A load-bearing seam with no stated warrant in its own row, held by a byte-sound ground available to the pair, is a warrant defect and not a disclosure gap: medium as filed. The proposed repair (argue the seam against MT 61:3's bytes, add oshb:Isa.61.3, treat observed_substrate_signals, rejected_alternative and confidence as dependent fields) stands with no seam movement.

MT 61:10 opens verse-initially on שׂ֧וֹשׂ אָשִׂ֣ישׂ בַּֽיהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier), the first-person-singular verb with its first-person chain continuing at נַפְשִׁי֙, הִלְבִּישַׁ֨נִי֙ and יְעָטָ֑נִי (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier), 'I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh!' (web:Isa.61.10), while MT 61:9 closes in the third person on כִּ֛י הֵ֥ם זֶ֖רַע בֵּרַ֥ךְ יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.61.9, byte tier); the row's rear-seam claim is byte-true. The shipped row's boundary_evidence_refs carries web:Isa.61.10 with no oshb:Isa.61.10, although every other web ref it cites (61:4, 61:6, 61:8) is paired with an oshb ref, and boundary_rationale quotes no Hebrew for the seam driver; the book-order neighbor row opening at 61:10 splices the identical run at byte tier. The SAMEKH keyed at MT 61:9 (single-witness, tier-3) corroborates and never drives. Same class and law as the 57:14 item: a load-bearing seam driver carried on the English witness alone fails the mandatory engagement class, a defective warrant with byte-true content, so the boundary is sound and nothing rises to high. Medium as filed; the proposed splice-and-ref repair stands with no seam movement.
